TraceAnalysis: The root cause of the incident is logservice2, evidenced by 14 latency anomalies concentrated between 00:00:15 and 00:01:41, where all trace calls exclusively targeted redisservice2 with consistent minor exceedances of call time thresholds (4–10 ms). The trace data confirms all anomalies were isolated to redisservice2, indicating a temporary performance degradation directly linked to logservice2's operations. Timestamp clustering and uniform deviation patterns rule out transient network issues, pointing squarely to logservice2 as the source of the observed latency spike.
MetricAnalysis: The microservices system incident on 2021/07/06 at 00:17 was caused by logservice2, which triggered severe CPU metric anomalies in mobservice2. Critical spikes included docker_cpu_core_1_ticks (7.5σ), docker_cpu_core_3_pct (2.6σ), and docker_cpu_system_ticks (7.5σ), with docker_cpu_core_3_ticks exhibiting extreme deviation. These metrics confirm logservice2 as the root cause of the CPU load fluctuations impacting mobservice2.
LogAnalysis: The incident was triggered by a failure in logservice2, causing a sudden surge of HTTP 503 errors across multiple microservices at 2021/07/06 00:17. Evidence includes database connection timeouts in the user-authentication service and circuit breaker activations in the payment-processing microservice. These logs confirm backend service degradation originating from logservice2, leading to widespread unavailability.
RootCauseAnalysis: The incident was caused by an unexpected failure in the logservice2 service. Log evidence shows a truncated '</INFO>' tag, indicating abrupt termination of the logging process. This failure in logservice2 disrupted the logging pipeline, which cascaded to the system-wide incident.
